## Goal

The host events log (~/gt/.events.jsonl) gets a `done` event for every submission, also from a sandbox seat, so the crash detector's done grace, the feed and `gt log` see sandbox submissions again. Today they see none: the log holds 649 `done` events and the last is 2026-10-29T01:46:10Z (bullet, a host seat).

Cause (read-only, egret): `gt done` writes the event at internal/done/done.go:1771 with events.LogFeed, which resolves the town root from the working directory (internal/events/events.go:185-232, workspace.FindFromCwd, then writeTo appends <townRoot>/.events.jsonl). A sandbox seat's town root is the rendered skeleton extracted at /sandbox/gt (internal/sandbox/skeleton.go; same finding as gt-8yk78 for spans), so the event lands in the sandbox's own file and is deleted with the sandbox. The timing matches the sandbox roll-out: the first sbx dispatch in daemon.log is 2026-10-28 20:15 CDT (01:15Z, sbx-haiku), host seats stopped taking beads at the 20:00 CDT close, and the last host-seat `done` is 01:46Z. Seats such as capable (30 done events before) now run in sandboxes and write none. gt-8yk78 already fixed the same gap for polecat spans by letting the host close the attempt from the submission the seat wrote into its READY TO LAND block; `done` was left out.

Fix: when the landing worker first sees a waiting submission, the host writes the `done` event the seat could not. The seam exists: landworker.Worker.FirstSight (internal/landworker/worker.go:67, recordSubmission at :500) is called once per submission with the land.Work (BeadID, Branch, Worker, Submitted), and the daemon wires land.SubmissionRecorder there (internal/daemon/landing_worker.go:762).

## Constraints

- Add a recorder in internal/land (a new file, e.g. done_event.go) with the same Record(w Work) (bool, error) shape, and a small composite so the worker's single FirstSight field runs both recorders. Wire it in internal/daemon/landing_worker.go:762 with the town root; no change to internal/landworker/worker.go unless the composite needs it.
- The event is `events.TypeDone`, actor `<rig>/polecats/<w.Worker>` (the seat form the crash detector compares, daemon.go ~3868), payload from events.DonePayload(bead, branch) plus `at`: the seat's own submission stamp w.Submitted when it is not after the host's first sight, else the first-sight time (the stamp may only pull the end earlier, the rule of closeSubmittedSpan in internal/land/landings.go). Written with events.LogFeedTo(townRoot, ...) so it never resolves a root from the working directory.
- No double events: skip when the log already holds a `done` event for the bead dated at or after w.Submitted minus a named constant of 15 minutes (a host seat writes its own just before its note). Read the log once and keep the keys, as SubmissionRecorder does.
- A crew submission (no polecat Worker) writes nothing. A failed write is returned as the error, which the worker already logs once and never lets hold up the landing.
- Read ~/.claude/docs/standards/test-engineering.md first. Temp directories and fake clocks only; no sleeps, no real town. No new GT_ environment reads.
- Do not change internal/done, internal/events, the spans code, or the overrun guard.

## Out of scope

Backfilling the done events missing since 2026-10-29T01:46Z; the dispatch clock (gt-3ga5l); other events a sandbox gt writes inside the sandbox (only `done` is read by a consumer today); sandbox log forwarding.

## Gate

Polecat gate: the narrow go test lines below. Owed by the overseer after install: submit from a sandbox seat and check ~/gt/.events.jsonl gains one `done` event for the bead with the seat actor within one landing-worker interval, and none for a host seat that wrote its own.

## Size

one worker, one landing

## Acceptance

- [x] TestDoneEventRecorderWritesTheSandboxSubmission: a land.Work with a Worker, branch and Submitted time, an empty temp events log, gives one `done` event with actor `<rig>/polecats/<worker>`, the bead and branch, and `at` equal to the seat's stamp; Record reports true; `go test ./internal/land -run 'TestDoneEventRecorder' -count=1` passes.
- [x] The same Work recorded twice writes one event, and a bead whose log already holds a `done` event within 15 minutes before w.Submitted (a host seat's own) writes none; both shown in the same `-run` form.
- [x] A stamp later than the first-sight time is replaced by the first-sight time, and a crew Work (no Worker) writes nothing, shown in the same `-run` form.
- [x] The composite runs both recorders and returns the first error without skipping the second: `go test ./internal/land -run 'TestFirstSightComposite' -count=1` passes.
- [x] The new tests fail when the dedupe window or the stamp rule is removed (checked by mutation, undone by exact text replacement, not git checkout), and `go test ./internal/land -run 'TestDoneEventRecorder|TestFirstSightComposite|TestSubmissionRecorder' -count=1` passes with them restored.

data.notes:
Implementation: internal/land/done_event.go adds DoneEventRecorder (payload events.DonePayload plus at = the seat stamp capped by the host first sight, actor <rig>/polecats/<worker>, written with events.LogFeedTo so no root is resolved from the working directory; skips a bead whose log already holds a done event inside the 15m doneEventDedupeWindow, and keeps a per-submission bead+stamp key so the per-pass record call cannot write twice under a skewed stamp). internal/land/first_sight.go adds FirstSightComposite, which runs every recorder and returns the first error after the rest have run. internal/daemon/landing_worker.go wires SubmissionRecorder and DoneEventRecorder under the worker single FirstSight hook. Tests: internal/land/done_event_test.go and first_sight_test.go. Mutations checked and restored by exact text replacement: doneEventDedupeWindow to 0 made TestDoneEventRecorderSkipsAHostSeatsOwnEvent red; dropping the at.After(now) cap made TestDoneEventRecorderCutsAStampPastTheFirstSight red; disabling the recorded key made TestDoneEventRecorderWritesOnceWithAStampPastTheFirstSight red. Gate: go test ./internal/land -run TestDoneEventRecorder|TestFirstSightComposite|TestSubmissionRecorder -count=1 ok; make build ok.

Rework (attempt 2) for the om findings on attempt 1:
- stale dedupe snapshot (major): DoneEventRecorder now keeps a byte offset and reads only the events log tail on every Record, so a host seat's own done event written after the daemon started is seen. A log rewritten shorter (prune) resets the offset and is read from the start. Tests: TestDoneEventRecorderSeesAHostSeatsEventWrittenAfterTheFirstRead, TestDoneEventRecorderReadsALogRewrittenShorter (mutation: restoring the load-once snapshot made the first red).
- unparseable done event (minor): a bead whose done event has no readable time is marked unjudged and Record fails closed with an error instead of writing a possible duplicate. Test TestDoneEventRecorderRefusesAnUnreadableDoneEventTime (mutation: dropping the mark made it red).
- seat-authored actor (minor): validSeatName bounds rig and worker to [A-Za-z0-9._-], at most 64 bytes, and Record refuses otherwise. Test TestDoneEventRecorderRefusesAMalformedSeat (mutation: skipping the check made it red).
- failed-write test (minor): the append goes through an injectable LogFeed seam (nil means events.LogFeedTo); the test injects the error instead of depending on the events lock-file name.
- typed nil recorder (info): nilFirstSight uses reflect to catch a typed nil pointer; TestFirstSightCompositeSkipsATypedNilRecorder (mutation: rec == nil panicked in it).
Checks: gofmt clean; go vet ./internal/land ./internal/daemon clean; go test ./internal/land -run TestDoneEventRecorder|TestFirstSightComposite|TestSubmissionRecorder -count=1 ok; make build ok. Rebased onto origin/main 63331d051; three-dot stat lists only the five files of this change.
Reader detail in the rework: refresh reads the whole .events.jsonl (the events_prune patrol caps it) but parses only the lines past the last offset, so a host seat's event written between passes is seen without re-parsing the log. A stored seam (the last parsed line) detects a rewrite under it (events_prune renames a shorter file over the log) and restarts from the top. The earlier note on this bead says tail-read; the I/O is a full read, the parse is the tail. Presubmit error-branch check: go test -coverprofile ./internal/land plus errbranch -base origin/main judged 7 of 7 added error returns, 0 findings.

OVERSEER GUIDANCE for attempt 3 (the third review rejection is mine, so fix the one major and the cheap infos completely): (1) MAJOR 152ecf: the Worker in the actor must not come from the seat-authored READY TO LAND block alone. The host knows who it slung: bd assignee of the bead is <rig>/polecats/<name> (set by the sling, not by the seat). Require validSeatName AND that w.Worker equals the last element of the bead assignee (and w.Rig the first); on mismatch Record returns an error and writes nothing. Test: a block naming another polecat as Worker is refused with nothing appended; mutation: removing the assignee check turns it red. Use whatever Work already carries or the existing bead lookup the landing worker uses; do not add a new bd call shape that needs the integration tier. (2) info 31336e / 180518 / b98ac8: leave, but state in the code comment that the tail-only read plus last-line rewrite detection is deliberate. (3) info a069ab: add one narrow test that the landing worker constructor wires a non-nil DoneEventRecorder (go test ./internal/daemon -run <narrow name>; container-suite package, narrow -run only). (4) info c9eb6a: validate BeadID/Branch with the same charset check or document why not. Keep the diff small; acceptance boxes only narrow go test -run commands.
